videos.title: Naming Acids and Predicting Acid Reactions | Year 12 Chemistry
videos.description:
Full lesson, notes and practice questions: https://hscscience.com.au/subjects/chemistry/year12/module6/lesson02.sa.html

Name any common acid from its formula: binary acids with hydro- and -ic, oxoacids from their ion (-ate to -ic, -ite to -ous). Then predict and balance the three acid reactions: with a hydroxide (salt and water), a carbonate (salt, water and carbon dioxide) and a reactive metal (salt and hydrogen). See why each product forms, why ammonia makes a salt with no water, why copper does not react with dilute acid, and how to tell carbon dioxide from hydrogen. Two exam-style questions at the end.

Chemistry 2017: Year 12 Module 6, Acid/Base Reactions.
Syllabus dotpoints (NSW Chemistry Stage 6, 2017, Module 6):
"investigate the correct IUPAC nomenclature and properties of common inorganic acids and bases (ACSCH067)"
"predict the products of acid reactions and write balanced equations to represent:
- acids and bases
- acids and carbonates
- acids and metals (ACSCH067)"
Official 2017 course: https://www.nsw.gov.au/education-and-training/nesa/curriculum/science/chemistry-stage-6-2017

Full lesson, notes and practice questions: https://hscscience.com.au/subjects/biology/year12/module7/lesson05.sa

Three plates: 3 colonies from tap water, 214 from a creek, none from a rainwater tank. Is the tank water safe? Is the creek full of disease? Design and run a microbial test of water or food properly: sterile sampling, aseptic technique, serial dilution, spreading, taping and incubating plates safely, and the negative and positive controls. Then choose the countable plate, calculate CFU per mL, and see what colonies can and can't tell you. Includes validity, reliability and accuracy, a risk assessment, and two exam-style questions with brief feedback.

Biology 2017: Year 12 Module 7, Infectious Disease. Inquiry question: "How are diseases transmitted?"
Syllabus dotpoint (NSW Biology Stage 6, 2017, Module 7):
"describe a variety of infectious diseases caused by pathogens, including microorganisms, macroorganisms and non-cellular pathogens, and collect primary and secondary-sourced data and information relating to disease transmission, including: (ACSBL097, ACSBL098, ACSBL116, ACSBL117)
- classifying different pathogens that cause disease in plants and animals (ACSBL117)
- investigating the transmission of a disease during an epidemic
- design and conduct a practical investigation relating to the microbial testing of water or food samples
- investigate modes of transmission of infectious diseases, including direct contact, indirect contact and vector transmission"
Official 2017 course: https://www.nsw.gov.au/education-and-training/nesa/curriculum/science/biology-stage-6-2017

Prerequisites: What makes a disease infectious? and How did experiments establish germ theory? Next: How does disease damage agricultural production?
